evaluations.evidence: entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the information needed to create a game (stakeholder need) rather than prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: inviting estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired way to invite participants (a link) but does not prescribe low-level UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget ('single multi-line text field') instead of stating the stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (to view all items) without prescribing implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user capability (select an item) rather than specifying how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States a required capability (edit items) without implementation-level detail.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder need (remove an item) rather than a specific solution.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the desired behavior/need without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete aggregation algorithm ('average') rather than stating the stakeholder need for a method to accept an estimate.

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an automatic implementation behavior (auto-filling a field) which is an implementation choice rather than a pure stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the user capability required without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a stakeholder need (re-estimate) rather than an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete storage/transfer format ('spreadsheet'), which is an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: References a specific format/method ('spreadsheet' and copy/paste) as the required solution instead of stating the need to get stories in bulk.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user's need (find previous games) without dictating implementation.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (see transcript) rather than specifying how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete storage/output format ('HTML file'), which is an implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete output format ('CSV file'), i.e., an implementation detail rather than the stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired outcome (removal of stored data) without prescribing how to implement deletion.

evaluations.evidence: entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the minimal user data required to create an account (stakeholder need) rather than low-level implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Describes the expected authentication action from the user's perspective without technical implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (update account data) rather than prescribing a solution.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the desired outcome (account deletion) without specifying implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a presentation preference (local timezone) as a stakeholder need, not a low-level implementation choice.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the delivery channel for a user-facing capability; although a mechanism, the channel is part of the stakeholder need (password recovery via email).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Defines domain options (estimation scales) rather than prescribing implementation mechanisms or UI widget details.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a capacity requirement (team size) and does not prescribe a technical or UI solution.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user action to join (enter name) and the access route (URL) without low-level implementation specifics.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States the user's need to view the item, not how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a viewing need without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired visibility of estimator actions; not prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the required behavior (simultaneous reveal) rather than low-level solution choices.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the allowed user interaction window; this is a functional need rather than an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need (view history) not tied to a specific implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Describes required visibility of who made estimates; not a low-level solution prescription.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a functional capability (timer and duration). Although it mentions a UI element (timer), it expresses the stakeholder's need rather than unnecessary implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired automatic behavior at the feature level (reset on condition) rather than a low-level implementation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: States the user's need to navigate history without prescribing specific UI controls.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a presentation consistency need rather than prescribing how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Defines an allowed user interaction (when changes are permitted) and not an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete UI elements (a thumbnail photo and its placement) instead of expressing the underlying stakeholder need in less implementation-specific terms.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete technologies/standards (XHTML and CSS), which are implementation choices rather than pure stakeholder needs.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States a content/knowledge need (glossary) and does not prescribe technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes an implementation-level optimization ('created database indexes') instead of stating the performance need.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete platform/version compatibility targets (implementation-level constraint) rather than the stakeholder need more generally.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes compliance with a particular standard/guideline (an implementation/solution choice) rather than stating the accessibility needs in purely stakeholder terms.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a non-functional stakeholder need (performance) without prescribing technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete technical encoding/format (Unicode) rather than expressing the stakeholder need more generally (use any language).

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Describes desired observable behavior (URL readability) without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: States a user-facing quality need (friendly error pages) rather than a low-level technical solution.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) without prescribing implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need (view usage metrics) and does not prescribe technical or UI implementation details.
